## What you will do

Compare mutation positions in an oncogene and a tumour suppressor, then write a
short report that combines evidence from at least three databases. **ELO 8, 9.**

Builds on [cell death beyond apoptosis](../regulated-necrosis/lec.qmd),
[cancer](../cancer/lec.qmd), the [disease casebook](../disease-casebook/lec.qmd),
and [the drug-journey capstone](../drug-journey/lec.qmd).
Allow about 3–4 hours for the guided activities; the independent report may need more time.

1. [In the browser: mutation patterns and death proteins](browser.qmd).
2. [In R: mutation positions in melanoma](report.qmd).
3. [Your own report: one mechanism, several sources](capstone.qmd).

## Before you start

No account is needed. Use RStudio or R with `rmarkdown`, `ggplot2`, `jsonlite` and
`httr2` installed. Install missing packages once in the console:

```r
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "ggplot2", "jsonlite", "httr2"))
```

Download the report and all listed snapshots. Put the report in a new folder and
CSV/JSON files in its `data/` subfolder. Keep the filenames. If an API is unavailable,
set `use_snapshot <- TRUE`. A snapshot is a dated copy of real records, not simulated data.
Knitting uses a fresh R session: create every object in the report and finish with
`sessionInfo()`. Do not include your R console history as a substitute for code.
